narrative.overview: The app is the pavement. Spots are marked the way crews mark the street, in flat utility locate paint, and the route to a spot is a dashed painted line on the ground. The shell is asphalt-black, the map ground is concrete grey, sheets are white, and type is stencil-cut condensed caps.
keyCharacteristics: Asphalt shell, concrete ground, white sheets.
Five flat paints, one per spot type; pink also means "go".
2px outlines on every control; pill and sheet radii.
Condensed uppercase display face for headings, buttons, labels; system face for reading text.
48px minimum targets; legible in direct sun.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Type Rule
rules.body: Orange, yellow, blue, green and white mean a spot type and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Go Rule
rules.body: Pink is the primary action and the route. One pink action per view.

rules.name: The Not-Hue-Alone Rule
rules.body: Type and difficulty always carry a text label; difficulty is marks plus text.

rules.name: The Stencil Rule
rules.body: Display face is always uppercase and used only for names, numbers, buttons and labels.

rules.name: The Flat-Fields Rule
rules.body: Fills are solid. Shadows are only for objects floating over the map, never for sheet content.

dos: Do colour spots only with the five paints through spotTypePaint, with a text label alongside.
Do outline every control and chip in 2px (white on asphalt, ink on light).
Do keep every target at least 48px and ink-on-paint text for contrast.
Do render the route as a dashed pink line and keep pink for the single primary action.
Do design for long strings, RTL and non-Latin fallback: let labels wrap or shrink instead of truncating the type chip.
donts: Don't use gradients, glows, or blur in new surfaces.
Don't use the paints for decoration or non-type state.
Don't set paragraphs in the display face.
Don't reintroduce the old navy and teal palette; the web client keeps its own look and is out of scope.
